name: Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle designed to travel on no more than three wheels, which expressly includes mopeds and electric motorcycles, whether powered by an electric motor or a combustion engine. Utah's traffic code has no separate motor-driven cycle category.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle for the rider and no more than three wheels on the ground; includes autocycles, mopeds and electric motorcycles
Not an electric assisted bicycle or a motor assisted scooter
The traffic code no longer has a motor-driven cycle category: H.B. 381 repealed it, so a light motorcycle that isn't a moped is simply a motorcycle
restrictions.citation: Utah Code §41-6a-102, as amended by H.B. 381 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Riders need a class D driver license with a motorcycle endorsement, except on a moped or autocycle
Riders under 21 must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting FMVSS 218 on a highway
Needs a headlamp, tail lamp, stop lamp, rear reflector, brakes, horn, mirror and road tires
Titled and registered with the Division of Motor Vehicles, with a registration fee each year
Entitled to full use of a lane
Lane filtering is allowed only past stopped traffic, at 15 mph or less, with two or more lanes in the same direction, on roads posted 45 mph or less or on off-ramps, never on-ramps
